correctness.rationale: The finite-field theorem follows from E[6]\E[3] = (E[2]\{0}) × E[3], because conic sections cut divisors linearly equivalent to 6O and all 3-torsion flexes have reducible osculating double lines. Collinear sextactic triples are exactly the three different nonzero 2-torsion components whose 3-primary coordinates sum to 0: hence 81 lines. For six distinct sextactic points the correct conic criterion is total group sum zero in E[6], and reducibility is equivalently a zero-sum triple partition. Independently enumerated all 296010 subsets of 27 points in (F_2)^2 × (F_3)^2, obtained 8244 zero-sum six-subsets, of which 2268 reducible and 5976 smooth. Enumerated all three universal Frobenius actions: full splitting has (2268,5976) rational reducible/smooth; order-three noncube has (36,0); involution case has (54,22), for 76 rational conics. Frobenius on E[2] from X^3=432 and on the flex E[3] then gives the 27/81 point/line cycle table, incidence and all finite-etale zeta products. Characteristic p≥5 is essential; enumeration establishes the finite group model, not finite-field generality independently of torsion geometry.
